clue.text: Vessel supplied with scurvy prophylactic, that's great!

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel
limes were issued to sailors to ward off scurvy

explanation.surface: Delight at a ship being stocked against scurvy.
explanation.walkthrough: British sailors were given lime juice against scurvy, hence their nickname 'limeys'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime is used informally as high praise, much like 'wonderful' or 'superb'.

clue.text: Upset, hurried one's cocktail

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: raced means hurried
one's is I plus 's, giving I and S

explanation.surface: A drinker, disturbed and rushing, orders a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses RACED + IS. The sidecar is a brandy and orange liqueur cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Take part in two sports by turns

explanation.surface: Someone alternates between two different sports.
explanation.walkthrough: Box and Cox is from a Victorian farce about two lodgers sharing a room in shifts; boxing and coxing a rowing boat are two sports.
explanation.definitionFit: To box and to cox are two athletic pursuits; the phrase also means alternately, in shifts.

clue.text: "This is perfect," thought the student

parts.note: an idea is a thought
L is the learner-driver plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A pupil thinks something is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the learner plates on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, as good as could be imagined.

clue.text: Site meant for redevelopment as a cafe

indicators.note: for redevelopment says the letters of site meant are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A plot of land earmarked to become a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for redevelopment' rearranges SITE MEANT. An estaminet is a small French cafe or bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or bistro.

clue.text: Slaver bringing back blackbird to the French

indicators.note: bringing back tells us to read the letters for black and bird from right to left

parts.note: split as black (B, as on pencils) plus bird
le is the French masculine form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A slave-trader returns a blackbird to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaver' looks like a slave-trader, but it is the verb meaning to let saliva run. 'blackbird' is read as B + BIRD, which 'bringing back' turns into DRIBB.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let spittle run from the mouth, the same as to drool.

clue.text: Nobles used to fight

explanation.surface: Aristocrats who settle things with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes are high-ranking peers; 'put up your dukes' uses the slang word for fists.

clue.text: Setting agent in sort of sailing ship

indicators.note: sort of says the letters are rearranged into another form

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A setting agent aboard some kind of sailing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges SAILING with SS. Isinglass is a fish gelatin used to set jellies and clear beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a gelatin from fish bladders used to set jellies and clarify drinks.

clue.text: Slattern with a broom

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman carrying a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: Besom is a dialect insult for a slovenly woman and also a broom made of twigs.

clue.text: Graceful poem unfinished by worker

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for poem loses its last letter

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A lovely verse left incomplete by a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the Y from ELEGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and refined in manner.

clue.text: Soldiers cook in this part of America

explanation.surface: A pot for army cooking named after a region of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: A dixie is a large military cooking pot; Dixie is also a nickname for the southern United States.

clue.text: Appropriate children argue the toss

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it
issue is a legal word for offspring

explanation.surface: Kids who seize things also quarrel about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb. 'Argue the toss' is a British idiom for disputing a decision already made.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute a point or object to it is a common idiom for contesting something.

clue.text: A hundred and fifty English scholars feast in February

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the word and given as it stands
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
MAs are Masters of Arts, graduate scholars

explanation.surface: A large party of English academics at a winter banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: Candlemas, the Christian feast of the Presentation, falls on 2 February.
explanation.definitionFit: This church festival, when candles are blessed, is held on the second day of the year's second month.

clue.text: Ancient letter, a survival from ogam, maybe

indicators.note: a survival is something remaining inside, so the letters survive within the words ogam, maybe

explanation.surface: An old character lingering on from the Celtic ogham script.
explanation.walkthrough: Ogam (ogham) is an early Irish alphabet, a neat cover for a Greek letter running across 'ogam maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The third character of the Greek alphabet, which dates from antiquity.

clue.text: Unsteady, or firm and unyielding

explanation.surface: Two opposite descriptions offered side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and wobbly is one sense; made of stone, and so hard and solid, is the other.

clue.text: Allow eyes to wander in the main

definitions.note: the main is an old poetic term for the open sea

indicators.note: to wander says the letters of allow eyes stray into new positions

explanation.surface: Let your gaze roam over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wander' rearranges ALLOW EYES. 'The main' is an old term for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The open ocean, in old poetic usage; this one is the body of water between China and Korea.

clue.text: The racing game?

parts.note: names a card game that shares its name with an English horse-racing town

explanation.walkthrough: The Suffolk town is the home of British flat racing, and a card game of the same name involves betting on cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game takes its name from the Suffolk town that is the headquarters of British horse racing.

clue.text: On one's toes in broad-brimmed hat

explanation.surface: Alert while wearing a hat with a wide brim.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide-awake means alert; it is also the name of a soft felt hat with a broad brim.

clue.text: Cut top off frill, causing a commotion

parts.note: a kerf is the cut made by a saw

indicators.note: top off means the word for frill loses its first letter

parts.note: a ruffle is a frill

explanation.surface: Trimming a frill causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' removes the R from RUFFLE, the first letter being the top in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a fuss or disturbance.

clue.text: One team entered in the race finally scratched, bewildered

indicators.note: entered in says the first two pieces go inside the race

parts.note: a plate is a horse race run for a prize
I is the Roman numeral for one
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of scratched

explanation.surface: A team pulled out of a race, leaving people confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered in' puts IXI inside PLATE; 'finally' adds the last letter of 'scratched'. Pixilated means bemused, as if led astray by pixies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixilated describes someone confused or bemused, as though pixie-led.

clue.text: Bird out of place? In place

indicators.note: out of place says the letters of in place are set in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Is the bird out of place, or in place?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird out of place' looks like the start of the anagram, but 'out of place' acts on the final 'In place'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large water bird with a throat pouch for scooping fish.

clue.text: Discard most of bark

indicators.note: most of means the word for bark loses its final letter

parts.note: to bark your shin is to scrape it

explanation.surface: Throwing away the greater part of a tree's covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like tree bark or a dog's noise, but it is the verb meaning to graze skin. 'most of' drops the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap something is to throw it away as useless.

clue.text: Quietly withdraw herald

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to recede is to withdraw

explanation.surface: A messenger discreetly backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano, the musical term for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to come before it, announcing its arrival.

clue.text: Rope, see, has caught the animal

indicators.note: has caught means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Look, the rope has snared the beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the animal' reads as a lassoed steer, but it is simply the donkey caught inside the old exclamation for 'look'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Bouquet delivered to an audience

indicators.note: to an audience signals the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: sent means delivered

explanation.surface: Flowers brought to a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers but is the smell of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its aroma, its smell.

clue.text: Insect bearing, 'tis said, supreme happiness

indicators.note: 'tis said signals the words before it are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a bee is an insect and attitude is bearing or posture

explanation.surface: An insect's poise is described as perfect bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE + ATTITUDE spoken quickly is heard as the word for blessedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatitude is a state of utmost blessedness or bliss.

clue.text: Move sprout up, say

parts.note: a bud is a young sprout

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Shift a shoot upwards, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift position slightly.

clue.text: Pig entered, switching places

indicators.note: switching places means the two halves of the phrase for entered swap round

parts.note: got in means entered

explanation.surface: A pig came in and swapped seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig' means pig iron, a block of cast metal, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig is an oblong block of cast metal, as in pig iron.

clue.text: Water-clock in dry places going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong says the letters of dry places are jumbled

explanation.surface: A water-clock fails in arid locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wrong' rearranges DRY PLACES. A clepsydra measured time by water dripping through a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A clepsydra is an ancient timer that measures time by the flow of water.

clue.text: Old man mostly responsible for faux pas

indicators.note: mostly means the word for old man loses its final letter

parts.note: gaffer is a British word for an old man

explanation.surface: An elderly fellow is largely to blame for a social blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaffer is British slang for an old man or a boss; 'mostly' drops its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or tactless remark.

clue.text: Fruit with an outer covering might be called bananas

definitions.note: a noun for someone described as bananas, slang for crazy

parts.note: a nut is a kind of fruit
a case is a covering around something

explanation.surface: A fruit in its shell might be named as a banana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit, which suits the surface, but it is slang for mad; someone so described is a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy, and a person thought crazy is called this slang noun.

clue.text: In the end, former member boards plane, perhaps

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: boards means gets on, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a plane is an example of a tree
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: Eventually an ex-MP gets on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the plane tree. 'boards' puts M inside TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: An extreme is the furthest point or limit of something.
